# Reflected outer fibers: one middle cap pays all missing slabs

This note proves an all-cap lower bound for a compatible family with two identical middle fibers and reflected outer pairs. the contributor proposed the multi-pair extension of the single-pair calculation; the disjoint-slab allocation below verifies it. No independent log-concavity of an allocated measure is assumed.

## 1. Collective theorem

Let d>=1, and let B be a full-dimensional convex body in R^d with centroid0 and volume b. Write mu for mixed volume and define the UNNORMALIZED depth by D_S(y)=inf_{H containing y} mu(H), where H ranges over closed ambient halfspaces. Its normalized depth is D_S(y)/M, where M=mu(S). Suppose an ACTUAL convex body has precisely the consecutive integer fibers

    K_0=K_1=B,
    K_{-k}=A_k,      K_{k+1}=-A_k,      1<=k<=N,        (1)

and no other nonempty integer fibers. Positive full-dimensional A_k may be assumed; the same fixed-d-volume argument permits lower-dimensional endpoint pieces when actual compatibility and completeness are retained. Put a_k=|A_k| and S=sum_k a_k.

Actual compatibility forces A_k,-A_k subset B. For every continuous normal u, the support roof h_z(u)=sup_{x in K_z}u·x is concave in the real base variable. Since h_0(u)=h_1(u)=h_B(u), all its exterior values are <=h_B(u). Applying this for all u proves the containments. Conversely, the containments alone are NOT asserted to prove compatibility of an arbitrary multi-pair prescription; actual compatibility is a hypothesis of (1).

The single actual mark(0,0) has every containing ambient closed halfspace of mass at least

    Gamma_d b+S,       Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.             (2)

Since total mass is M=2(b+S), this gives

    D_S(0,0)/M >= Gamma_d/2
                +(1-Gamma_d)S/[2(b+S)].              (3)

The same conclusion holds at(1,0), by reversing the base order and exchanging A_k with -A_k. The centering condition is essential to the use of ordinary Grünbaum: the reflected outer pairs in (1) must be reflected about the centroid of the common B. An arbitrary marked reflection center is not silently identified with that centroid.

## 2. One cap, one disjoint allocation, all outer pairs

Write a nonvertical through-(0,0) cap as

    u·x >= t z,        u!=0.                           (4)

The own B fiber at0 contributes at least Gamma_d b. The other middle fiber at1 contributes |B intersect{u·x>=t}|.

The two kth outer traces have total mass

    |A_k intersect{u·x>=-kt}|
        +|A_k intersect{u·x<=-(k+1)t}|.               (5)

If t<=0, their two scalar ranges cover the real line, so (5)>=a_k independently for every k. The desired outside contribution S is already obtained.

If t>0, the only uncounted portion of A_k lies in

    E_k=A_k intersect{-(k+1)t<u·x<-kt}.

Thus (5)>=a_k-|E_k|. Reflection preserves volume and maps E_k to

    -E_k subset (-A_k) intersect{kt<u·x<(k+1)t}
          subset B intersect{kt<u·x<(k+1)t}.          (6)

The open bands in (6) are pairwise disjoint and all lie in the SAME other-middle cap{u·x>=t}. Consequently

    sum_k |E_k| <= |B intersect{u·x>=t}|.              (7)

Adding (5) over k and adding that one middle-cap mass proves the outside contribution is at least S. Together with the own ordinary Grünbaum contribution this proves (2) for every nonvertical through-point cap. Boundary hyperplanes have zero d-volume, so closed/open band endpoints do not affect the calculation.

A pure base cap through0 contains the whole own B and at least one side of complete endpoint pairs, of massS; it therefore has mass at least b+S>=Gamma_d b+S. Every containing cap includes a parallel through-point cap. This completes the all-halfspace proof, including pure-base boundary mass.

The proof is collective: (7) spends each portion of the other middle cap at most once. Summing independent single-pair payments would not supply this conclusion.

## 3. Exact four-fiber theorem with a symmetric middle

For N=1, suppose B=-B and A is any full-dimensional convex body contained in B. The four fibers

    A, B, B, -A       at0,1,2,3                      (8)

are actual: their canonical convex hull is contained in R times B, so the two prescribed B fibers cannot enlarge, and the endpoint bases expose exactly A and -A. These are all the integer bases of the projection.

At(1,0), translating the proof above by one base unit gives the lower bound b/2+a, because every own B cap through its center has exactly half the volume. To prove a matching GLOBAL upper bound, fix a nonzero continuous normal u and choose L sufficiently large that

    ±u·x-L(z-1)>=0                                   (9)

each contains the whole A fiber at0, cuts the B fiber at1 in half, and misses fibers2,3. Both cap masses are b/2+a. Their margins sum to-2L(z-1), so their union covers every continuous plane over z<=1.

Similarly

    ±u·x+L(z-2)>=0                                   (10)

each has mass b/2+a and the pair covers every plane over z>=2. Thus (9)-(10) cover every old candidate, and indeed all integer planes globally. We have the EXACT maximum

    Q=b/2+a,       beta=(b/2+a)/[2(b+a)].             (11)

Every endpoint's maximum is at most a/2 by the opposite-cap bound, so the endpoint fibers are not deepest. The two actual middle centers attain Q. No finite-menu assumption replaces the all-normal lower proof.

## 4. A finite decreasing contraction, including point endpoints

Choose any anchor c in A and put

    A_t=c+(1-t)(A-c),        0<=t<=1.                (12)

Then A_t subset A subset B and -A_t subset B. The four canonical fibers A_t,B,B,-A_t remain actual for the same reason as (8). Their endpoint volumes are a_t=(1-t)^d a. Formula (11) holds for every t<1 and also at t=1 with the zero-dimensional endpoint points c,-c assigned d-volume zero:

    beta(t)=(b/2+a_t)/[2(b+a_t)],
    d beta/d a_t=b/[4(b+a_t)^2]>0.                  (13)

Therefore beta strictly decreases as the endpoint mass decreases, and its final value is1/4. The point endpoints have zero depth by pure-base exposure and do not create hidden competing candidates. They may then be pruned without changing the positive mixed measure.

For more than one reflected outer pair, independently shrinking all A_k need not preserve the adjacent support-roof inequalities. No such multi-pair deformation is inferred from the collective cap payment.

## 5. Every centrally symmetric four-interval array belongs to the contraction class

In continuous dimension one, suppose four consecutive positive interval fibers form an actual body symmetric under (z,x)->(3-z,-x), after translating the symmetry center. Their two middle intervals have the same length. A measure-preserving affine shear can make both of their centers zero. The shear itself is odd about z=3/2, so it preserves the reflected relation between the two outer intervals. Thus the new middle fibers are one centered interval B and the endpoint fibers are A,-A.

The concave upper and convex lower endpoint sequences, constant across the two middle bases, force A,-A subset B. The exact theorem and finite contraction (11)-(13) therefore apply to EVERY centrally symmetric four-interval array, not only centered profiles(a,b,b,a).

This class has an actual coordinated contraction even when the geometric preserving-birth set at every new integer base is empty, as in `candidate f66dcff3eb3e1f03`. It is a proved restricted alternative, not a universal birth-or-contraction theorem for arbitrary sources.

# Reflected outer fibers: one middle cap pays all missing slabs

**Collective slab payment for reflected outer fiber pairs**

For an actual convex-body source with exactly the consecutive fibers B at bases 0 and 1 and reflected outer pairs A_k,-A_k at bases -k,k+1, centered so the reflection center is the centroid of B, every cap through that central centroid receives at least Gamma_d |B|+sum_k |A_k|. For positive base tilt, missing pieces map to disjoint open bands in the other central fiber; pure-base cuts retain boundary mass.

Scope limits: Requires the stated reflected geometry and full-dimensional B, d>=1. This is not an intrinsic-degeneracy reduction. Independent contraction of many outer pairs is not asserted.
